newsitem.title: ITALY: Separatist Bossi to declare northern independence.
newsitem.headline: Separatist Bossi to declare northern independence.

text.p: Separatist leader Umberto Bossi geared up for the grand finale of his cross-Italy march to declare "independence" for his would-be northern state on Sunday but rivals dismissed the move as a flop.

Two pro-unity demonstrations at points along the River Po, a focus of Bossi's three-day trek, were planned by centre-left and Green parties to counter his declaration of a separate state of "Padania".
Bossi has said millions of supporters will flock to Venice for the proclamation. His Northern League party has drawn a parallel with the U.S. declaration of independence in 1776.
On Saturday, the fiery leader appealed for calm then promptly announced he wanted to set up a militia and would fight for independence.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has dismissed Bossi's secessionist campaign as "a ridiculous game".
The Northern League won a surprising 10.6 percent in Italy's general election in April but a new opinion poll showed only 7.6 percent of Italians favoured secession and 85.6 percent were opposed.
Gianfranco Fini, whose far-right National Alliance plans a pro-unity demonstration in central Milan, said Bossi's performance so far was "a flop".
Several thousand supporters turned up at Bossi's rallies on Saturday but the numbers were embarrasingly short of the tens of thousands predicted by his party.
Nevertheless, Bossi made sure he grabbed attention with his speeches.
"The world should know that Padania is stirring and there is no longer any tolerance," he said.
"If force is needed, and it is possible that it will be needed, from Monday the provisional government will take care of that with the voluntary recruitment of a national guard."
His announcement came in the wake of an overnight bomb attack on a Northern League office in Venice. No one was hurt and damage was slight but Bossi accused Italy of firing the first shot.
He was careful to temper his fighting talk, especially after ugly scenes in Turin on Friday night when far-left youths stoned his supporters, injuring about a dozen.

"Tomorrow should be a day of holy peace, a happy day," he said, drawing on the quasi-religious symbolism that has been central to the three-day campaign that began with a ritual collection of water from the Po's Alpine source to represent the birth of his "state".

Audiences for Bossi's rallies were outnumbered by the turnout for a pop concert in the mediaeval town of Mantua, his planned "capital" and seat of his self-styled parliament. The city is governed by Prodi's centre-left Olive Tree coalition.
Some 6,000-10,000 people packed the town square for the concert, which was also attended by the mayor of Naples. Flags in Italy's red, white and green were prominent in the crowd.
Bossi said "Padania" would have to live with two governments for a year but the Italian one would steadily lose support.
"It will be a year of great battle, of great demonstrations and there is no doubt that Padania will win," he said.
Italy in its current state was like "a house built half on a swamp and half on a rock", he added.
Centre-left Naples mayor Antonio Bassolino, whose speech raised the loudest applause at the Mantua concert, gave Bossi short shrift.
"There's no room for Bossi's racist madness," he said.
